title: "Owner of the Day of Judgment"
hookLine: a day when every account is settled, held by the one just named merciful
carry: the account is in kind hands
tomorrow: "Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help"

cards: A shopkeeper's ledger has two columns: what came in, and what went out. Most of a life never makes it into a ledger. Dishes washed that weren't yours.
An angry text deleted before it was sent. A night spent sitting up with someone, never mentioned again. Nobody writes the quiet things down.
And on the other side, the things nobody caught. Today's verse says both columns are kept. Dropped into a prayer about mercy, that can sound like a warning.

teach.h: YAWM AD-DIN — THE DAY OF THE ACCOUNT.
teach.b: Verse four: “Owner of the Day of Judgment.” In Arabic, maliki yawmi d-din. Today's word is the day itself: yawm ad-din.
Yawm is day. And din, translated judgment, is also the everyday Arabic word for religion, a way of life.

At its root it carries the sense of a debt coming due, an account settled. So this is the day when every account is squared: both columns, the unseen good and the unfinished wrong. Now, where it sits.
Praise, then mercy, then mercy again, and only then the Day.

teach.h: HELD BY THE ONE NAMED MERCIFUL.
teach.b: The one just named merciful, twice, is the one who holds the account. Some readers take that order as the point: the reckoning isn't in the hands of a stranger, or an enemy, or a machine. It's held by mercy.
And in that reading, nothing quiet is lost: the dishes, the unsent message, the night beside someone. In the conversation from day two, God answers this verse too: My servant has glorified Me.
Some tellings add: My servant has entrusted his affairs to Me. Read that way, the verse isn't dread.

how: Muslims say this verse in every unit of every prayer. Belief in the Last Day is one of the articles of faith in Islam.

games.q: what's inside verse four — tap the pairs.
p: judgment, religion, a debt coming due
the unseen good, the unfinished wrong

s: this verse comes before any mention of mercy
it comes after mercy is named twice: in verse one and verse three.
din can also mean religion, a way of life
the same word: and at its root, a debt coming due.
in the conversation hadith, God answers this verse with a threat
My servant has glorified Me; some tellings add: My servant has entrusted his affairs to Me.

games.q: in the conversation hadith, someone praying says: Owner of the Day of Judgment. how does God answer?
games.why: My servant has glorified Me; some tellings add: My servant has entrusted his affairs to Me. not a threat, a handing-over.

practice: Sit comfortably. Bring to mind one good thing you did that nobody noticed. Let it be small.
Hold it, and let it be enough that it happened. Then one thing you'd like to settle well: an apology, a debt, a promise. Don't solve it.
Just set it down in front of you, honestly.

wordCard.voice: Yawm ad-din. The Day of Judgment, held by the one just named merciful. Fourteenth word. Salaam, the five pillars, salat, alhamdulillah, Rabb, rahma, yawm ad-din: that's week two.

orig.note: Arabic: the Day of Judgment. din also means religion, a way of life, and carries the sense of a debt coming due.

carryVoice: Your line: the account is in kind hands. Nothing quiet is lost. Two weeks, done.
